modelAnswer: The counter-current multiplier mechanism and hormones work together to concentrate urine and maintain water balance. The counter-current multiplier in the Loop of Henle creates an osmotic gradient by actively transporting sodium and chloride ions from the thick ascending limb into the medulla, while the descending limb remains permeable to water. This establishes a concentration gradient that allows water reabsorption. Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) enhances this process by increasing the permeability of the collecting duct to water, enabling more water reabsorption along the osmotic gradient established by the counter-current multiplier. modelAnswer: Hemophilia, colorblindness, and muscular dystrophy are X-linked recessive genetic disorders with distinct inheritance patterns. Hemophilia results from deficiency of blood clotting factors (VIII or IX), affecting primarily males who inherit the recessive allele on their single X chromosome, while carrier females are typically unaffected. Colorblindness (red-green) follows similar X-linked recessive inheritance, with affected males (XcY) and carrier females (XCXc) showing the characteristic pattern. Muscular dystrophy, particularly Duchenne type, is also X-linked recessive, causing progressive muscle degeneration in males due to absence of dystrophin protein. All three disorders demonstrate that affected males cannot pass the condition to sons (sons receive Y from father), but all daughters of affected males become carriers, illustrating the critical role of X-chromosome inheritance in these genetic diseases.
